brief.situation: You are the network engineer at Fennick Outdoor. At 10:12 a pricing job published the limited jacket JKT-LTD-01 at 0.99 instead of 99.00. The pricing team fixed it at the origin at 10:20, but shoppers still see 0.99 and orders at that price keep arriving. The Black Friday banner goes live at 11:00 and sends ten times the traffic to the store.
handover: The storefront is behind an external Application Load Balancer with Cloud CDN on backend bs-store (URL map um-store).
Price responses carry Cache-Control: public, max-age=86400 (set years ago for 'static' prices).
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows the CDN's cached copies, the fixed origin and the shoppers in between.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

writeup.question: For the record: why shoppers kept seeing 0.99, what you invalidated and why not everything, and what changes.

parts.label: Why
parts.modelAnswer: The origin returned 99.00 since 10:20, but the CDN had cached the 0.99 response at 10:12 with max-age 86400 and answered every request from that copy.

parts.label: Invalidated
parts.modelAnswer: The two paths from the publish log, /api/prices/JKT-LTD-01 and /products/jkt-ltd-01. Invalidating /* would have sent the banner's ten-times traffic to an origin that survives on a 96% hit ratio.

parts.label: Changes
parts.modelAnswer: Price responses now cache for 60 seconds, and the pricing runbook lists the paths to invalidate after a correction.

originDown.headline: Invalidate what is wrong, not everything
originDown.body: The bad price was on two paths. A targeted invalidation fixes them; a full one removes the cache the origin needs at peak, as the documentation warns.

bannerWrong.headline: A fixed origin is not a fixed cache
bannerWrong.body: With max-age one day, the CDN serves its copy until it expires. Invalidate the affected paths.

invalidated.headline: Good: a targeted invalidation
invalidated.body: You confirmed the origin was right and the CDN stale, found exactly which paths carried the price, invalidated only those, checked the price and the origin load, and shortened the TTL.

scoring.modelReasoning: The origin is correct and the CDN is serving a copy cached with a one-day max-age. Invalidate only the two paths that carry the price; the CDN refetches them and keeps everything else, so the origin's load hardly changes. A full invalidation before a ten-times traffic spike removes the cache the origin depends on; republishing at the origin does nothing for cached copies. Shorten the price TTL and give the pricing team the path list.
